ov: A sure-footed, white-coated climber of the high mountains of western North America, often seen on near-vertical cliffs. Despite its name it is not a true goat: its closest relatives are goat-antelopes such as the chamois. It stays high up, where few predators can follow.
rg: Mountains of western North America, from Idaho and Montana through British Columbia and Alberta to southern Yukon and southeastern Alaska.
df: Grasses, herbs, sedges, ferns, mosses, lichens, and twigs and leaves of shrubs and conifers.
fx: British Columbia holds half of the world’s mountain goats.
Kids weigh just over 3 kg at birth and try to run and climb within hours.
